([[Summerville, South Carolina]]) | college = [[Furman Paladins men's basketball|Furman]] (2018–2023) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | highlights = * [[Southern Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|SoCon Player of the Year]] (2023) * [[Southern Conference|SoCon]] Defensive Player of the Year (2022) * 2× First-team All-SoCon (2022, 2023) }} '''Jalen Slawson''' (born October 22, 1999) is an American basketball player who recently completed his college career for the [[Furman Paladins men's basketball|Furman Paladins]] of the [[Southern Conference]]. He is a [[2023 NBA draft]] prospect. ==Early life and high school== Slawson grew up in [[Summerville, South Carolina]] and attended [[Pinewood Preparatory School]].{{cite web|url=https://www.postandcourier.com/journal-scene/sports/slawson-steps-into-leadership-role-for-panthers/article_98243259-5c3f-5965-b144-1a72ad4ddb81.html|title=Slawson steps into leadership role for Panthers|work=[[The Post and Courier]]|date=January 17, 2017|access-date=March 16, 2023}} He was named the Area Player of the Year after averaging 14.6 points, 10.5 rebounds, 4.1 blocks, and 3.5 assists per game as a senior.{{cite web|url=https://www.postandcourier.com/our-gazette/sports/prep_sports_awards/prep-sports-slawson-named-boys-basketball-player-of-the-year/article_6c60b48a-b38f-5ad5-bcac-634d3a58ed08.html|title=PREP SPORTS: Slawson named Boys Basketball Player of the Year|work=[[The Post and Courier]]|date=May 9, 2018|access-date=March 16, 2023}} Slawson committed to play college basketball at Furman.{{cite web|url=https://www.postandcourier.com/journal-scene/sports/pinewood-prep-hoopsters-sign/article_a5e72814-c127-53fc-80bf-f6c1cf5ac708.html|title=Pinewood Prep hoopsters sign|work=[[The Post and Courier]]|date=November 13, 2017|access-date=March 16, 2023}} ==College career== Slawson was a key bench player during his freshman season at Furman and became a starter entering his sophomore year. He averaged 8.7 points as a junior.{{cite web|url=https://www.greenvilleonline.com/story/sports/college/furman/2022/02/18/jalen-slawsons-summerville-sc-furman-basketball-bob-richey/6829947001/|title=Jalen Slawson's bond with coach Bob Richey key to Furman basketball|work=[[The Greenville News]]|date=February 18, 2022|access-date=March 16, 2023}} Slawson was named the [[Southern Conference]] (SoCon) Defensive Player of the Year and first-team All-SoCon after averaging 14.4 points, 7.4 rebounds, 3.7 assists, 2.5 steals, and 1.7 blocks per game during his senior season.{{cite web|url=https://www.greenvilleonline.com/story/sports/college/furman/2022/10/31/furman-basketball-socon-favorite-must-handle-hype/69595537007/|title=Furman basketball is the SoCon favorite. Now it must handle the hype|work=[[The Greenville News]]|date=October 31, 2022|access-date=March 16, 2023}} Slawson decided to utilize the extra year of eligibility granted to college athletes who played in the 2020 season due to the coronavirus pandemic and return to Furman for a fifth season.{{cite web|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/colleges/2023/03/15/ncaa-tournament-furman-mike-bothwell-jalen-slawson/1367d736-c360-11ed-82a7-6a87555c1878_story.html|title=Furman found NCAAs thanks to college roommates, best friends|work=[[Washington Post]]|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|date=March 15, 2023|access-date=March 16, 2023}} He was named the [[Southern Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|SoCon Player of the Year]] as he helped lead the Paladins' to their first NCAA tournament appearance in 43 years.{{cite web|url=https://www.postandcourier.com/sports/college/sapakoff-jalen-slawson-the-heart-of-furmans-ncaa-tournament-joy/article_bfbe93f2-c195-11ed-b5b3-976854f9cbda.html|title=Jalen Slawson, the heart of Furman's NCAA Tournament joy|work=[[The Post and Courier]]|date=March 14, 2023|access-date=March 16, 2023}} ==Personal life== Slawson's father, Tom Slawson, played college basketball at the Citadel.{{cite
